subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Arabic term “Adl” means:
explanation: Adl, justice, is the central aim of Islamic governance; the Qur’an repeatedly commands it.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: “Amr bil Ma’ruf wa Nahi anil Munkar” means:
explanation: It is a collective duty of the Muslim community and the basis of the institution of Hisbah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: “Siyasah Shar’iyyah” refers to:
o: Governance and public policy within the objectives and limits of the Shariah
explanation: It is the discretionary policy of rulers in the public interest, provided it does not contradict the Shariah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: When sending Hazrat Ali (RA) to Yemen as a judge, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) told him not to decide a case until he had:
o: Heard the other party as he heard the first
Taken an oath from the witnesses
explanation: Hearing both sides fully is a basic principle of fair trial in Islamic law.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) described the best Jihad as:
o: A word of truth before an unjust ruler
explanation: The hadith encourages speaking truth to power, a form of public accountability.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to a hadith, a ruler who dies while deceiving the people under his charge will be:
explanation: The hadith warns that betraying public trust is a grave sin for any person in authority.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: When the people of Kufa complained against their governor Hazrat Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas (RA), Hazrat Umar (RA):
o: Sent an inquiry and later replaced him
explanation: Umar had the complaints investigated in Kufa’s mosques; though Sa’d was cleared, he was replaced to maintain public confidence.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to a hadith, the ruler (Sultan) is the guardian of:
explanation: The state assumes responsibility for orphans, the destitute and others who lack a guardian.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Khutbat-ul-Wida (the Farewell Sermon) was delivered at:
explanation: The Prophet delivered the sermon at Arafat during Hajjat-ul-Wida, near Jabal-ur-Rahmah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Farewell Sermon declared that an Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab except by:
explanation: It proclaimed that all people descend from Adam, and only righteousness distinguishes one from another.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In the Farewell Sermon the Holy Prophet (PBUH) declared sacred, like the sanctity of that day and month:
o: The life, property and honour of the believers
explanation: He made each person’s blood, wealth and honour inviolable, a foundation of human rights in Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In the Farewell Sermon, the first Riba declared abolished was that of:
explanation: The Prophet began by cancelling the interest owed to his own uncle Abbas, showing that reform starts with one’s own family.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Regarding women, the Farewell Sermon instructed men to:
o: Leave their maintenance to their fathers
Treat them kindly, for they have rights over you
explanation: The Prophet reminded men of their duties to their wives and to fear Allah in their treatment of women.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Khutbat-ul-Wida is often described as:
explanation: Its declarations on equality, life, property, honour, women’s rights and justice make it a comprehensive statement of human rights.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’anic teaching that killing one innocent person is like killing all mankind emphasises:
explanation: Surah Al-Ma’idah makes the value of every single life equal to that of all humanity.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’anic principle “There is no compulsion in religion” establishes:
explanation: Faith must be accepted freely; no one may be forced to embrace Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’anic prohibition of “tajassus” (spying) protects the right to:
explanation: Surah Al-Hujurat forbids spying on others and backbiting, safeguarding people’s private lives and honour.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’anic statement “We have honoured the children of Adam” establishes:
o: The dignity of every human being
explanation: Human dignity belongs to all people by virtue of their humanity, regardless of race, religion or status.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to the Qur’an, mankind was made into nations and tribes so that they may:
explanation: Surah Al-Hujurat adds that the most honoured in Allah’s sight is the most righteous, rejecting racial pride.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Cairo Declaration on Human Rights in Islam (1990) was adopted by the member states of the:
explanation: The OIC adopted it to set out human rights from an Islamic perspective.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’anic command “Let not the hatred of a people lead you to be unjust” requires:
explanation: Surah Al-Ma’idah commands justice as nearer to piety, even when dealing with those one dislikes.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Islam encouraged the emancipation of slaves by, among other things:
o: Making it an act of expiation (Kaffarah) for certain sins
explanation: Freeing a slave was made an expiation for sins such as breaking an oath or accidental killing, and a highly rewarded virtue.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The hadith warning that whoever kills a Mu’ahid will not smell the fragrance of Paradise protects:
explanation: A Mu’ahid is a non-Muslim with a covenant of protection; his life is inviolable under Islamic law.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Under the Charter of Madinah, the Jewish tribes were guaranteed:
o: Freedom to practise their own religion
The right to choose the Prophet’s successor
explanation: The Charter declared that the Jews have their religion and the Muslims theirs, within one community of Madinah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: When the Holy Prophet (PBUH) stood up as a Jewish funeral passed and was told it was a Jew’s, he replied:
o: “He was a neighbour of Abu Bakr.”
explanation: His reply shows respect for every human being regardless of religion.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to the Seerah reports, the Christian delegation of Najran was allowed to:
o: Pray in their own way in Masjid-e-Nabawi
explanation: Ibn Ishaq reports that the Prophet let them offer their prayers in his mosque, an often-cited example of religious tolerance.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The verse “For you is your religion and for me is mine” is from Surah:
explanation: Surah Al-Kafirun rejects any compromise in worship while leaving others to their own religion.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet’s saying that he would cut off the hand of even his daughter Fatimah if she stole emphasises:
explanation: When people interceded for a noblewoman of Banu Makhzum, he said earlier nations perished because they punished the weak and spared the powerful.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said “He who cheats is not of us” after finding hidden defect in:
o: A heap of grain in the market
A bag of dates given as charity
explanation: He put his hand into the grain and found it wet beneath, and condemned concealing defects from buyers.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) commanded that a labourer be paid:
o: At the end of the year
explanation: Prompt payment of wages is a basic right of the worker in Islamic teaching.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) praised earning by one’s own hands and cited the example of:
o: Hazrat Sulaiman (AS), who ruled a kingdom
Hazrat Dawud (AS), who ate from the work of his hands
explanation: Though a king, Dawud (AS) lived on what he earned by his own craft, showing the dignity of labour.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an likens backbiting (ghibat) to:
o: Eating the flesh of one’s dead brother
explanation: Surah Al-Hujurat uses this image to show how repugnant backbiting is.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’anic declaration “The believers are but brothers” lays the foundation of:
explanation: Surah Al-Hujurat commands believers to reconcile between brothers, making brotherhood a social duty.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The hadith of the woman punished for starving a cat and the man forgiven for giving water to a thirsty dog teaches:
explanation: Mercy and cruelty to animals carry reward and punishment in Islam.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Islamic teachings on war prohibit:
explanation: The Prophet forbade killing women and children, and his caliphs extended protection to the elderly, monks, crops and animals.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to a well-known hadith, Paradise lies under the feet of:
explanation: The saying stresses that serving one’s mother is a path to Paradise.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: When asked who most deserves good treatment, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) said “your mother” three times, and then:
explanation: Repeating “your mother” three times before the father shows the special right of the mother.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an forbids saying even “uff” (a word of contempt) to:
explanation: Surah Bani Israil commands kindness to parents, especially in their old age.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: What is meant by “Sila-e-Rahmi”?
explanation: Sila-e-Rahmi is joining and maintaining relations with relatives; severing them is a grave sin.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an describes husband and wife as “garments” for one another, meaning that they:
o: Protect, comfort and cover each other’s faults
explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah uses the image of a garment for closeness, protection and mutual support in marriage.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an states that women have rights over men:
o: Only after the age of forty
Similar to those men have over them, in fairness
explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah affirms reciprocal rights and duties between spouses according to what is fair.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Islam, the responsibility for providing Nafaqah (maintenance) of the family rests primarily on:
explanation: The husband must provide food, clothing and housing for his wife and children even if the wife has wealth of her own.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In an Islamic marriage, Mahr is:
o: A gift that is the right of the wife
A payment to the bride’s father
explanation: The Qur’an commands husbands to give their wives their Mahr willingly; it belongs to the wife alone.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Islam, the marriage of an adult woman requires:
explanation: The Prophet said a previously married woman must be consulted and a virgin’s consent sought; a forced marriage could be annulled.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to the Qur’anic command on adoption, an adopted child is to be called by:
o: The name of the adoptive father
The name of his real father
explanation: Surah Al-Ahzab ordered adopted children to be known by their biological fathers, preserving lineage.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an condemned the pre-Islamic Arab practice of:
explanation: Surah At-Takwir says the buried girl will be asked for what sin she was killed, condemning female infanticide.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Among the rights Islam gave women, which was widely denied in pre-Islamic Arabia?
explanation: The Qur’an fixed shares for daughters, wives, mothers and sisters, whom the Arabs had often excluded from inheritance.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Islam, a married woman’s own property and earnings:
o: Remain her own and under her control
Must be given to the state
explanation: Islam gives women an independent legal and economic identity; the husband has no claim on her wealth.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an declares that men and women who do righteous deeds with faith:
o: Will be rewarded according to lineage
Will be rewarded in this world only
explanation: Whoever does good, male or female, while believing, will be given a good life and full reward.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The hadith “Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim” applies to:
explanation: The obligation to acquire essential knowledge falls on every Muslim, male or female.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that he and the one who looks after an orphan will be in Paradise:
o: If the orphan is a relative
explanation: He joined his index and middle fingers to show how close the carer of an orphan will be to him.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said Jibrael kept advising him about the neighbour until he thought the neighbour would be made:
explanation: The hadith shows the great emphasis Islam places on the rights of neighbours.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In the Farewell Sermon, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) abolished blood feuds of the Jahiliyyah, beginning with the blood claim of his own family for:
o: The son of Rabi’ah bin al-Harith
explanation: By renouncing his own clan’s claim first, he set an example of ending cycles of revenge.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The verse “Indeed Allah commands justice, excellence and giving to relatives”, often recited in the Friday sermon, is from Surah:
explanation: Surah An-Nahl contains this comprehensive command of Adl, Ihsan and kindness to kin, with a prohibition of indecency and oppression.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hazrat Umar (RA) is reported to have fixed an allowance from the Bait-ul-Mal for an elderly non-Muslim he found begging, showing that:
o: State welfare extended to non-Muslim citizens
explanation: The report, given by Abu Yusuf, is cited to show that the Islamic state cared for its needy non-Muslim subjects too.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: When Hazrat Abu Dhar (RA) taunted a man about his mother’s race, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) told him:
o: “You are a man in whom there is still Jahiliyyah”
explanation: The rebuke shows that racial contempt belongs to pre-Islamic ignorance.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an forbids Muslims to revile the deities others worship because:
o: They may in turn revile Allah out of ignorance
It is permitted only in war
explanation: Surah Al-An’am teaches restraint and respect in religious discourse.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: When a Companion wished the Holy Prophet (PBUH) to witness a gift made to only one of his sons, the Prophet:
o: Refused and told him to treat his children equally
Asked him to give it to the eldest
Told him to donate it to the treasury
explanation: In the case of Nu’man bin Bashir he said, “Fear Allah and be just among your children.”

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to a hadith, the truthful and trustworthy merchant will be with:
o: The prophets, the truthful and the martyrs
explanation: Honesty in trade is raised to the rank of the highest virtues.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that the best among you are those who are:
explanation: He added that he was the best of them to his own family.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to the Holy Prophet (PBUH), the strong person is the one who:
explanation: True strength is self-control in anger.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’an praises those who, for the love of Allah, feed the poor, the orphan and the:
explanation: Surah Ad-Dahr includes prisoners among those whom believers feed, establishing humane treatment of captives.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) promised a special reward in the Hereafter for one who:
o: Brings up daughters with care until they are grown
explanation: Raising daughters well, in contrast to the pre-Islamic contempt for girls, was declared a path to Paradise.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: When women asked the Holy Prophet (PBUH) for time to learn, he:
o: Told them to learn from their husbands only
Fixed a separate day to teach them
explanation: He set aside a day to teach the women, showing their right to education.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In Islam, the remarriage of widows is:
o: Allowed only with the tribe’s consent
explanation: Islam rejected customs that barred widows from marrying again; most of the Prophet’s wives were widows or divorcees.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that he was sent to:
explanation: Moral excellence (akhlaq) is presented as the purpose of his mission.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to a hadith, if a Muslim plants a tree and people or animals eat from it:
o: He must pay Zakat on it
It counts as charity for him
explanation: The hadith encourages cultivation and care for the environment as a continuing good deed.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Bait-ul-Hikmah (the House of Wisdom) was established in:
explanation: The Abbasids developed the House of Wisdom in their capital Baghdad as a library and centre of translation and research.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Bait-ul-Hikmah reached its height under the Abbasid caliph:
explanation: Al-Mamun expanded it and sponsored scholars and translators, making it the leading intellectual centre of its time.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The chief activity for which Bait-ul-Hikmah is remembered is:
o: Translating Greek, Persian and Indian works into Arabic
explanation: Scholars there translated and built upon works of philosophy, medicine, mathematics and astronomy.
